messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> oncall-julie: ELB health checks failing in us-west-2b for model-serving ELB (svc-model-prod-elb). Marking SEV1 if not acknowledged in 5m.

oncall-julie: acked. I'm oncall — grabbing cloudwatch metrics and recent deploys.

sara chen: seeing elevated 5xx from the ELB target group in us-west-2b, 5m error rate ~12%. us-west-2a looks normal.

gabe thomas: I can confirm cross-AZ latency spike and some instance network errors — kernel packet drops reported in recent dmesg on a subset of EC2s. Possibly an AZ-level networking degradation.

oncall-julie: copying logs to thread.
```
03:12:42 target/instance i-0abcd... HTTP_502 70%
03:12:45 kernel: vxlan0: tx timeout, resetting
03:13:01 ntp: peer unreachable
```

ops-lead: tagging this as potential AZ networking event — start mitigation: fail traffic away from us-west-2b to 2a and 2c where we have capacity.

rebecca - cust success: FYI: two customers (custom-dedicated clusters) reported timeouts from their webhooks. I'm pre-notifying them that we're investigating and may route traffic.

oncall-julie: attempting immediate Route53 failover by lowering weights for us-west-2b record-set. Also disabling targets in the ELB for 2b to let clients drain.

sara chen: pls run this to check target health quickly:
```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:targetgroup/tg-svc-model/abcd
```

oncall-julie: ran describe-target-health — many i-0* show Unhealthy with health reason TCP_CONN_ERROR. I'm deregistering all 2b targets to prevent 502s.

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic canary routing engaged — traffic will shift per policy to us-west-2a up to 60% in 5m increments.

gabe thomas: I pushed a temp autoscaling policy to spin up fresh instances in 2a/2c with the same launch config and health hooks. Should increase healthy capacity to accept shifted traffic.

oncall-julie: Opened AWS support case 1234567890 for "Networking degraded in us-west-2b impacting EC2 and ELB." Saw a STATUS: Investigating from AWS console.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support: We have an active investigation for EC2/ENI issues in us-west-2b. ETA for initial update 30m.

ops-lead: runbook checkpoint: 1) Notify customers (done) 2) Shift DNS weights (in progress) 3) Drain and deregister 2b targets (done) 4) Add temporary autoscaling capacity (done) 5) Monitor error rate and latency.

rebecca - cust success: Notifying impacted customers with guidance: retry/backoff and we will follow up with RCA.

sara chen: Observing initial improvement after deregistering 2b targets — error rate dropped to ~3% in 10m, latency normalizing. Still seeing rare 502s for sessions pinned to 2b (sticky sessions).

oncall-julie: Forcing session purge on ELB for affected apps via deregister and re-register should clear stuck sessions. Doing a rolling replace of the remaining 2b instances' ENIs.

g abe thomas: small correction — typo earlier: gabe.

gabe thomas: After purge and shift, p50 latency back to baseline and 5xx under 1% cluster-wide. We'll keep the routing policy in place until AWS confirms recovery.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> mitigated. Continue monitoring; if error rate <1% for 30m, we can move to monitoring-only.

ops-lead: Assigning temporary post-incident actions: - run network-level health checks for ENI drops quarterly - add an extra AZ buffer for high-throughput model endpoints - refine Route53 failover thresholds for faster shift.

rebecca - cust success: Customers updated. Two asked for ETA on full restoration — told them we'll wait for AWS confirmation before reintroducing 2b.

oncall-julie: leaving a note for on-call handoff: I'll be available for the next 25m, then hand to sara. Key facts: AWS case 1234567890, DNS weights shifted, 2b targets deregistered, error rate normal.

sara chen: taking over monitoring. Will run a validation sweep across all target groups and ASGs for any lingering UNHEALTHYs.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support: Update: Root cause appears to be intermittent networking fabric congestion in us-west-2b impacting ENI attachments; fix is in progress. We will provide follow-up once fully restored.

ops-lead: closing update: mitigation successful, no config rollbacks needed. Will schedule a postmortem and include customer impact table and timeline.

rebecca - cust success: Requesting that PMs prepare a short customer-facing post-incident note — cc: product.

sara chen: Logging timeline and attaching relevant CloudWatch graphs into the incident ticket.

gabe thomas: thumbs up.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED -> monitoring-only. If any regressions, reopen thread. :white_check_mark:
